Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Power Generation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Power Generation's Q3 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer, and David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mark Johnson.

Mark Johnson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by:
    1. Key achievements and navigating challenges effectively during the quarter.
    2. Continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio.
    3. Strong earnings per share performance and its key drivers.
    4. Positive progress on our regulatory rate case filings and outcomes.
    5. Clear earnings guidance for the next quarter and full year.

These elements highlight our resilience and strategic positioning. Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss the financials in greater detail, including these areas.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Mark. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.68 and revenue of $2.82 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on renewables and clean tech initiatives as part of our $1.8 billion deployed year-to-date. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate continued momentum supporting our full-year outlook and 8-10% long-term EPS CAGR.

Before moving on, let me provide deeper insight into the five key drivers Mark highlighted, starting with our key achievements and challenges during the quarter, which underscore our resilience in a dynamic utilities and power generation landscape. We delivered strong operational and financial results amid volatile wholesale markets, regulatory tailwinds from the Inflation Reduction Act, and escalating demand from data centers and electrification trends.

On the financial front, consolidated revenues rose 11% year-over-year to $2.82 billion, fueled by a 7% increase in retail sales volumes to 28.5 million MWh and higher wholesale power prices averaging $45 per MWh across our ERCOT and PJM footprints, up from $38 per MWh last year. Adjusted EBITDA reached $850 million, up 15%, with margins expanding 220 basis points to 42.5%, thanks to our optimized generation mix and lower fuel costs. Natural gas prices averaged $2.85 per MMBtu for our fleet, down 18% year-over-year, and with our 68% gas-fired capacity providing a fleet-wide heat rate of 7,650 Btu per kWh, we capitalized on merchant opportunities. Our trading desk captured $120 million in optimized dispatch value through real-time bidding in MISO and SPP markets.

Operationally, we achieved commercial operation on our 450 MW Desert Sun Solar Plus Storage project in California's Imperial Valley, integrating 200 MWh of Tesla Megapack battery storage for four-hour firming capacity. This brings our total renewables portfolio to 4.2 GW, with solar capacity factors improving to 28.5% through advanced bifacial panels and tracker optimization. In wind, our 300 MW repower at the Prairie Winds farm in Oklahoma boosted output by 22% to 1.1 million MWh using GE 2.8-MW turbines with extended tip speeds. These moves position us ahead of California's 60% RPS mandate and deliver $75 million in IRA production tax credits this year.

In Texas ERCOT, extreme heat drove peak demand to 85 GW, running our 2.5 GW gas fleet at 92% capacity factor for $250 million in uplift revenues. In PJM, we secured FERC approval for a 150 MW synchronous condenser at our Susquehanna nuclear uprate, supporting 15% year-over-year load growth from hyperscalers like AWS and Google. Customer satisfaction hit 88%, with SAIDI down 5% to 85 minutes via AI-driven predictive maintenance on 45,000 miles of T&D lines.

Our $1.2 billion capex advanced the GridFlex 2030 initiative, including $400 million in DERMS for 500 MW of virtual power plants, aligning with $50 million DOE grants for HVDC interconnects to enable 1 GW offshore wind by 2026.

Challenges included Hurricane Elena's landfall on the Gulf Coast, causing a 72-hour outage at our 1,200 MW combined-cycle plant in Louisiana, curtailing 150,000 MWh and costing $45 million. Overall availability dipped 4% to 91%, though quick SCR catalyst replacements limited NOx issues. Supply chain delays for transformers and turbine blades pushed our 200 MW Atlantic Offshore project 45 days to Q1 2025, with lead times at 18 months amid tariffs on Chinese modules; we countered with $30 million in U.S.-made First Solar contracts, but O&M rose 8% to $220 million from labor and steel inflation.

Regulatory and financing pressures featured rising rates lifting our blended debt cost to 5.2% after a $500 million green bond, trimming ROE by 50 basis points. PJM capacity prices fell 12% to $110 per MW-day due to coal retirements, affecting our 800 MW fleet, and ERCOT queues hit 250 GW, delaying 300 MW solar. Yet our balance sheet holds $1.8 billion liquidity and 3.1x net debt-to-EBITDA, fueling our $6 billion backlog with cost discipline targeting 2-3% OpEx cuts via drones and GenAI.

Q3 demonstrated execution amid volatility, renewables at 35% of mix, data center contracts up 40% year-over-year, setting up 8-10% EBITDA growth in 2025.

Moving to our investments in renewable energy and the clean energy transition—a cornerstone of our long-term value creation. With our diversified fleet of traditional baseload thermal assets and a rapidly scaling renewables portfolio, we're positioned to capitalize on decarbonization mandates, tech cost deflation, and policies like the IRA and EU's REPowerEU.

In the first nine months of 2024, we deployed $1.8 billion in capex toward renewables and clean tech, 42% of our $4.3 billion annual guidance, up from 32% in 2023. This added 1.2 GW online: 750 MW utility-scale solar PV, 350 MW onshore wind, and 100 MW standalone BESS. Our renewables now total 8.7 GW nameplate, contributing $1.1 billion in trailing twelve-month adjusted EBITDA, up 28% year-over-year at 11.2% average post-tax IRR.

Performance shines: solar at 26.5% capacity factors in ERCOT and CAISO, with co-located BESS cutting curtailments 65% and adding $150 million annual ancillary revenue. Wind at 38% in Midwest despite soft regimes. LCOE for new solar-plus-storage at $32 per MWh, eyeing $28 by 2026.

Our $500 million Horizon Hybrid program integrates solar, wind, BESS—like the 400 MW Desert Bloom in Arizona with NextEra bifacials, GE Vernova inverters, and 200 MW/800 MWh Fluence Mosaic at 92% round-trip efficiency for PG&E RA mandates. Offshore, 300 MW Atlantic Breeze off Virginia with Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines hits first power Q4. Green hydrogen pilot at legacy PJM coal site: 50 MW electrolyzer targeting $40/kg by 2027 with Plug Power.

In U.S., ERCOT added 500 MW solar amid 10 GW queue, with 15-year PPAs at $35 per MWh for Google, Meta. CAISO BESS wins $300 million against duck curve. PJM renewables offset 12% peak, FERC 2222 adds $80 million DER. Internationally, 20% in Enel Green Power's 1 GW Iberian solar for CBAM, Australian 400 MW wind at 12% IRR via Capacity Investment Scheme.

Renewables now 45% contracted capacity, up from 35%, 85% new builds in 15-year investment-grade PPAs at $40-45 per MWh vs. MISO-South merchant gas. IRA 45X credits added $120 million Q3, transferability speeds hyperscaler deals. ESG: MSCI AA rating drew $2 billion green bonds at 75 bps.

Pipeline: 10 GW, 60% advanced, 2.5 GW ops 2025 with $2.2 billion capex, $600 million EBITDA at 10-12% IRRs. Interconnection reforms, supply localization mitigate risks; CCUS on gas bridges to net-zero 2040.

These fuel earnings, resilience, Nexus leadership.

Next, our earnings per share performance and drivers, a standout this quarter validating our diversified portfolio. Adjusted EPS hit $1.68, beating guidance midpoint $1.60 and consensus $1.62 by 3.7%, up 18% from Q3 2023's $1.42 and 5% from Q2's $1.60. GAAP EPS $1.55; YTD $4.92 tracks to full-year $5.40-$5.60, ahead of street $5.35.

Drivers: 65% from organic revenue, merchant optimization.

Regulated rate base in Southeast (2.5M customers Georgia/Carolinas) added $0.08 EPS from 2023 PSC settlement, 9.8% ROE on $12.4B base; CDDs 15% above normal lifted demand 4.2%.

Wholesale PJM/ERCOT (8 GW gas/battery): PJM BRA $270/MW-day up 40% yielded $250M capacity, $0.12 EPS; Texas LMPs $45/MWh on data centers, peakers/BESS $80M uplift, 25% margin gain.

Renewables: 400 MW CAISO solar-storage $0.05 accretion at $32/MWh LCOE; IRA 45X $0.03.

Headwinds $0.10: gas $2.80/MMBtu up 20% -$0.04 (70% hedged $2.40); O&M +7% -$? turbine costs; D&D/interest $0.03/$0.03 from capex/debt (AFUDC $25M offset); regulatory/weather -$0.02.

Reconciliation excludes $0.13 non-recurring: $40M FTR gain, $25M ash reserve. Core +15% YoY.

Validates Reliable Clean Growth: coal retirements (3x600 MW by 2025) to 1.5 GW CCGT/800 MW wind/solar for RPS. $8B five-year capex: $1.5B HVDC, $500M BESS. EVs 1,200 MW peak, AI data centers fuel 6-7% regulated growth.

Southeast 45% earnings 10% growth; Texas/PJM 30% upside; CA renewables hedge. Q4 EPS $1.45-$1.55, FY reaffirm. Risks gas/FERC, upsides auctions/IRA.

Now, updates on regulatory rate case filings and outcomes, foundational to our $15.2 billion five-year capital plan, 60%+ to clean transition/grid resilience. Timely relief recovers renewables/BESS/transmission amid rates, chains, electrification.

Midwest (2.8M customers Ohio/Indiana): Q2 PUCO filing $285M on $12.4B base, 10.75% ROE. Oct 15 final: $238M (83% ask), 10.25% ROE +75 bps. Full smart meters $450M AMI-2, 90% wildfire capex. Unlocks 250 MW MISO BESS Phase 2 with 800 MW solar; 4.2% 2025 EPS.

Texas ERCOT (22% base, 1.2M customers): Q1 PUCT formula $420M on $18.7B, transmission for 40 GW renewables 2030. Sep 20 full approval 10.4% ROE, true-up, resiliency rider $150M microgrids post-Uri, NERC CIP-014; timely for 5-7% CAGR loads data centers.

California (15% earnings): CPUC GRC Dec $1.2B on $22B, 11.0% ROE. ALJ proposed $920M/9.8% ROE, prudence on 15% $300M DER/VPPs NEM 3.0. Contesting briefs; pivoted $75M wildfire LiDAR. VPP aggregates 120 MW/45k batteries.

Florida FPSC Aug $180M (95%) on $9.8B, 10.2% ROE funds 1.2 GW solar-storage, 300 MW Sweetwater First Solar for IRP.

Pipeline: Kentucky MYRP $350M formulaic; Indiana $110M modernization; FERC $4.5B PJM 11.5% ROE for 2 GW offshore.

85% capex PBR reduces volatility; ROEs +50-100 bps YoY as regulators see net-zero capex ($2T US 2030). 65% renewables 2027 for decoupling/CCUS. YTD $1.1B relief +12% guidance, consolidated ROE 10.1%, 6-8% EPS.

Finally, forward-looking guidance for Q4 and full FY 2024, grounded in momentum across regulated/competitive segments. Fleet: 12 GW gas CC, 8 GW renewables (wind/solar), 3 GW nuclear, 1.2 GW storage in PJM/ERCOT/SPP.

Q4 revenues $2.75B-$2.85B, 8-12% seq from Q3 $2.82B? Wait, strong ERCOT prices >$150/MWh peaks, data center PPAs 90% factors. Gas fleet 92% avail Q3, guide similar, 85% gas hedged $3.25/MMBtu.

Adj EBITDA $850M-$900M vs Q3 $850M, 250-300 bps to 32%; $120M renewables full Desert Sun ramp 450 MW solar/200 MWh Tesla 95% RTE. Reg rate base $28B-$29.5B, FERC 10.2% ROE, Illinois case 100% grid capex.

Q4 diluted EPS $0.98-$1.05 >consensus 3-5%, opex tight 7,200 Btu/kWh gas, non-fuel O&M $45/kW-yr flat, deferred $50M outages.

FY24 raise: revenues $10.8B-$11.0B +5-7% YoY; EBITDA $3.35B-$3.45B +9% 31.5% margins; $450M merchant PJM nuclear 93% CF, $300M renewables PTC/ITC 45X.

FY EPS $3.92-$4.02, +$0.22 mid, 15% competitive gen. Offsets $75M weather NE, offset data centers 5.5 GW PPA backlog 70% fixed >12% IRR.

2025 capex $2.8B: 40% renewables 30% storage 20% nuclear 10% CCUS; 1 GW green H2 SPP coal site DOE/45V mid-2026. ERCOT 6-8% CAGR EVs/crypto; PJM capacity $120/kW-mo 95% clear.

Risks: gas >$4, FERC MISO delays 800 MW wind, cyber ($100M NERC CIP-013). Confident AFFO $4.10, 4.2% dividend, $500M buyback. Assumes stable weather/commodities/reg.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our gas-fired power plants due to the implementation of AI-driven predictive maintenance and advanced heat rate optimization. This has resulted in a 15% increase in output while maintaining high availability above 92% across the fleet.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the green hydrogen space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth, complementing our renewables push and positioning us for the net-zero transition.

Mark Johnson: Thank you, John, Lisa, and David. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Mike Ross with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Ross: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for further investments in renewables and clean energy?

Mark Johnson: Certainly, Mike. As John outlined in detail, our renewables strategy is robust with $1.8 billion deployed YTD, 1.2 GW added, and a 10 GW pipeline targeting 2.5 GW in 2025. We're focusing on hybrids like Desert Bloom and green hydrogen pilots to drive 10-12% IRRs while de-risking with PPAs and tax credits.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: What is your outlook for EPS in the coming year?

John Ramirez: Thanks, Emily. We're on track for FY24 EPS of $5.40 to $5.60, with Q4 at $1.45 to $1.55 adjusted. Looking to 2025, we see 8-10% growth supported by rate relief, renewables accretion, and merchant upside, assuming stable commodities.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Lee: How are you mitigating risks related to regulatory outcomes and supply chain issues?

Lisa Chen: Good question, Tom. On regulatory, we've secured $1.1 billion YTD relief at improving ROEs, with 85% capex under PBR. Supply chain-wise, we're localizing with U.S. manufacturers like First Solar, forward contracting, and advancing GridFlex for resilience, as seen in our BESS and VPP deployments.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Mark Johnson for closing remarks.

Mark Johnson: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3 2024, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Nexus Power Generation for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Nexus Power Generation.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
